text:
marta: Heads-up: cost alert from telemetry yesterday — spike in span volume from checkout routes. We need a pragmatic sampling UX and runtime plan that supports per-route + tenant tiers.
ryan: Can you paste the alert? is it tail-heavy (errors/latency) or just high QPS?
marta: Mostly steady QPS increase after the promo, but tail spans around payment time are noisy. Alert: `spans_ingested_per_min` up 4x for route:/checkout/submit for tenant org-42.
sasha: This is exactly the place for combined head/tail sampling: keep head for first N spans/seconds, then selectively tail-sample based on latency/error signals.
ryan: Agree. Two important constraints: (1) deterministic sampling so we don't split traces across services, (2) runtime configuration must be API-first and support canarying.
infra-bot: Deploy pipeline note: changing sampling rules will be global config in control-plane v2; rollout uses feature-flagging and traffic-cuts.
devex: From console side we should expose an "estimated retention cost" preview when editing sampling rules so PMs can see impact before applying. Also a simple per-route toggle + advanced JSON policy editor.
alex: Proposal sketch: sampling policy model that composes rules: route match -> tenant tier -> head retention (seconds or count) -> tail sampler (deterministic hash + condition). Example: 

```
{
  "route": "/checkout/*",
  "tenant_tiers": {
    "gold": {"head_keep_secs": 30, "tail_policy": {"type": "latency_tail", "threshold_ms": 300, "rate": 0.2}},
    "standard": {"head_keep_secs": 10, "tail_policy": {"type": "error_tail", "rate": 0.05}}
  },
  "fallback": {"head_keep_secs": 5, "tail_policy": {"type": "probabilistic", "rate": 0.01}}
}
```

sasha: That looks good. A few finer points: deterministic tail sampling should use `trace_id % 10000 < X` kind of bucket so we keep cross-service traces intact. Also need to ensure parent-less spans from async workers are handled.
ryan: We should export sampling decisions as attributes on the span (e.g., `redwood.sampling=kept/head/tail/remote`) so downstream tools and exports know what was done. Useful for billing and correctness.

marta: What about exporter behavior? If a tenant has strict retention on certain spans, we might need to route their raw spans to a longer-retention exporter (S3/BigQuery) while serving reduced throughput to hot ES cluster.
infra-bot: Exporter note: adding a column `sampling_tier` to OTLP export via resource attributes is straightforward. But watch out for increased egress — we need quota gating.

devex: Console UX ideas:
- per-route quick presets: "Aggressive cost", "Balanced", "Full fidelity (trial)"
- a slider with live token/span reduction estimates and cost delta
- ability to preview rules applied to sample trace IDs (simulate)

alex: For canary we should support percentage rollout by tenant or by route prefix. e.g., rollout 10% of traffic to new sampling policy for "gold" tenants only.
sasha: Also add metrics: sampled_vs_total_by_route, head_kept_count, tail_kept_count, discarded_count, CPU cost estimate. We'll need those in console for debugging regressions.

ryan: Edge cases:
- If a trace spans multiple routes with different rules, deterministic trace-level decision wins. We should compute a trace-level decision at the ingress span and propagate.
- Batching/backpressure: if exporter queue fills, don't silently drop; mark spans `redwood.drop_reason=queue_overflow` and emit alert.

marta: Good. Who owns the runtime change vs control-plane and console?
alex: Runtime (eng-runtime) for deterministic sampling and span attribute exports. eng-platform for control-plane APIs and rules engine. devex for console. infra (ops) for exporters/quota gating.

devex: Quick mock for the console policy editor (text):
"""
Create policy for /checkout/*
[Preset dropdown] [Tenant tier mapping table] [Head keep: 30s] [Tail sampler: latency > 300ms -> keep 20%] [Preview impact] [Canary: 5% tenants] [Save & rollout]
"""

marta: Action items:
- alex: write runtime design doc for deterministic trace-level decision and span attribute tagging (due Tue).
- ryan: design Control Plane API schema + canary semantics (due Wed).
- devex: wireframe console cost preview and preset UX (PT).
- sasha: define metrics spec for sampled vs total and failure modes.

ryan: One more technical detail: for deterministic hashing use SHA1(trace_id) mod 10000 rather than raw trace_id to avoid skew with non-uniform IDs.
sasha: +1. Also remember to include a toggle for "force keep errors" so any span with `status.code >= 2` can bypass sampling if customer opts in.

marta: Thanks all — this is starting to feel actionable. I'll create a GH epic and link these tasks. :rocket:
alex: FYI I'll add a small simulation harness to estimate end-to-end retention before we touch prod rules.
infra-bot: Note: I scheduled a short meeting to align exporters and quotas tomorrow 10:30.
ryan: Cool. If nobody objects I'll start the API PR draft after the design doc.
devex: No objections. :thumbsup:
